chunks: A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Haytham ibn Waqid, from Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah Al-Arjani, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who prays in his house, then goes to a mosque from their mosques, and prays with them, will emerge with their rewards.

key_terms.مَسَاجِدِهِمْ: Their mosques (referring to the general mosques of Muslims)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying a prayer at home and then repeating it in congregation at the mosque?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies that performing a prayer individually followed by the congregational prayer (*Jam'at*) results in cumulative rewards rather than redundancy. The phrase 'exits with their good deeds' signifies that the individual retains the full reward of the solitary prayer while simultaneously acquiring the collective merit of the congregation, a principle often discussed in the context of *Salat al-Fard* (obligatory prayer). This ruling underscores the high value Shia scholars place on congregational worship as a means of enhancing individual spiritual standing.

en.hubeali:
A group, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Haysam Bin Waqid, from Al Husayn Bin Abdullah Al Arjany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who prays a Salāt in his house, then goes to a Masjid from their Masjids (of the general Muslims), so he prays Salāt with them, would come out with their Rewards (for himself)’.
en.sarwar: 8. A group has narrated from has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from form al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Haytham ibn Waqid from al-Husayn ibn ’Abd Allah al-Arjaniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one performs Salah (prayer) in his house then comes to one of their Masjid and performs Salah (prayer) with them, he leaves with all of their good deeds.’”
